name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a server-side skip link at the top of every page that jumps to the main content. This works without JavaScript and fixes keyboard navigation for users who rely on it. The trade-off is a small extra server request, but it’s worth it for universal access.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s server-side skip link risks cluttering every page load for sighted users who don’t need it. A better fix is a conditional skip link that only appears after keyboard navigation starts—this keeps the benefit for keyboard users without the constant visual noise. Settle it by testing with screen-reader users: if the skip link appears too late or feels intrusive, drop it; if it’s invisible until needed, keep it.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a server-side skip link at the very top of every page, visible by default. Keyboard users need it immediately—no delay, no JavaScript dependency. The trade-off is a tiny extra server load for all users, but that’s negligible compared to the barrier a missing skip link creates. This isn’t about sighted users; it’s about ensuring keyboard navigation works from the first keystroke.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s visible skip link fails sighted users who tab once—it flashes an irrelevant element before they reach their target. A hidden skip link that appears only after the first tab press solves this without JavaScript, keeping the benefit for keyboard users and the clean page load for everyone. Test it with screen-reader users timing their first tab press—if it’s under 200ms, the risk is real.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a hidden skip link that appears only after keyboard focus, tested for contrast and reduced motion. Owner: Ramp.
